FINDING_ID: CODX_R4_CONV_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1571) and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1645), single-linkage clustering is combined with an all-or-nothing novelty test at the class level. That lets a “bridge” finding hide a genuinely new member of the same class. I reproduced this with `A~B`, `B~C`, `A!~C`: round 1 becomes one class `['B','C']`, `_novel_classes(1)` returns `[]`, `kappa_set(1)=1.0`, and `_veto(1)=False` even when `C.severity=0.95`. The new severe issue is therefore treated as if it never happened. Because [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5048) forwards only `novel_classes` into Area 5, the same false-negative also propagates into diminishing-returns logic.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute novelty per finding before class aggregation, or switch to a clustering rule that cannot merge members unless the whole cluster is mutually above `tau_sim` (for example complete-linkage or clique-based grouping). Add a regression test for the `A~B`, `B~C`, `A!~C` case and assert that the novel severe finding still triggers veto.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CODX_R4_CONV_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1630) and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1680), cumulative classes are re-clustered from scratch every round, and each cluster keeps only `max(severity)`. A late bridge finding can therefore merge two previously distinct historical classes and make cumulative severity go down when a new finding is added. I reproduced: round 1 cumulative severity was `1.7` from classes `['A']` and `['C']`; after adding a low-severity bridge `B`, round 2 cumulative severity dropped to `0.9`, `_novel_classes(2)` became `[]`, and `kappa_set(2)=1.0`. That is a monotonicity break: more evidence should not erase previously counted issue mass.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Freeze historical class partitions once established, or use an aggregation scheme whose cumulative denominator cannot shrink when new findings arrive. Add a regression test asserting that cumulative severity mass is non-decreasing across rounds.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CODX_R4_CONV_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1472), two same-class findings with empty descriptions are assigned similarity `0.8`, which exactly matches the default `tau_sim=0.8` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L120). Since `Finding.description` defaults to `""` at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L347), blank findings auto-collapse into duplicates by default. I reproduced a case where a new blank finding with severity `0.95` produced `_novel_classes(2)=[]` and `_veto(2)=False`. So extraction failure or omitted descriptions can masquerade as convergence and suppress the high-severity stop guard.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Treat empty or near-empty descriptions as non-comparable unless a separate structured signature exists. At minimum, make empty/empty similarity fall strictly below `tau_sim`. Add regression tests for empty-description findings across rounds and assert that blank severe findings remain novel unless explicitly linked.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: CODX_R4_CONV_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: At [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1546), `add_round_findings()` defaults `adoption_delta` to `0.0`, and [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1727) interprets missing data as perfect adoption stability (`kappa_adopt=1.0`). The same default is exposed at [dynamic_management.py](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4963). I reproduced a run with no adoption deltas ever supplied where round 2 returned `kappa_set=1.0`, `kappa_rate=1.0`, `kappa_adopt=1.0`, and `converged=True`. That means the advertised three-metric conservative combination silently degrades to a two-metric detector whenever the caller forgets or cannot compute `Delta_r`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `adoption_delta` optional and distinguish “missing” from real zero. If absent, either block convergence or require an explicit config flag to ignore the adoption metric and emit a warning. Add a regression test asserting that omitted adoption data cannot yield `converged=True` silently.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
